goal: Design and implement executable cross-validation and bounded feedforward inside the real Provider project-generation lifecycle while preserving formal evidence, packaging, and delivery authority boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Every newly generated and checkpoint-reused component produces a current hash-bound cross-validation receipt before downstream publication.
The receipt cross-binds frozen plan paths, actual files, component quality receipt, implemented interface registry, upstream completion, and passing upstream receipts.
Only a verified passing receipt creates the bounded projection embedded in the next integration feedforward snapshot.
The assembled project produces an aggregate receipt before the existing post-build stage.
Failure blocks or uses the existing component quality repair route and cannot create a second generation path.
The receipts remain veto-only support state and cannot assert formal evidence, package, deliver, or replace canonical test/runtime/visual gates.
Positive, tamper, missing-path, missing-upstream, component-loop integration, management validation, and kernel guard tests pass.

quality_metrics.measure: cross-view consistency and safe downstream publication during real project generation
quality_metrics.target: 100% of generated and reused components have hash-valid plan/quality/interface/upstream receipts before publication, only passing bounded projections feed downstream, and one aggregate receipt exists before post-build
quality_metrics.method: deterministic positive and negative receipt tests, component-loop integration test, artifact/event-log inspection, and kernel authority guard

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

prevention: Define stage position, independent views, failure behavior, bounded output, and authority exclusions before integration.
assurance: Review the design against the kernel mainline and local_packager-only exit.
Verify checkpoint reuse is revalidated and downstream context receives no failed projection.
Review support status and formal EvidenceStatus separation.
control: Run deterministic receipt tests including tamper and missing-upstream cases.
Run a mocked real component-generation loop with artifacts and event logs.
Run management validation and kernel contract guards.
improvement: Record experience usage outcomes and retain post-build evidence convergence as a separate future increment only if it does not duplicate canonical gates.

interface_expectations: scripts/cross_validation_feedforward.py owns deterministic receipt and projection construction without Provider, packaging, or delivery calls.
scripts/run_local_pipeline_impl.py invokes the receipt after component quality validation for new and reused components and before component publication.
CGKNIntegrationFeedforwardSnapshot.upstream_state carries only bounded verified passing projections.
The aggregate receipt is written before post-build continuation while canonical evidence and local_packager remain unchanged.

feedback: Deterministic and integration evidence passed, and a real qwen3-coder-plus run produced two passing component receipts with verified upstream-to-downstream feedforward; the Provider failed later at the existing split-test anchor contract before aggregate post-build evidence.

worked: Separating the four independent views in one hash-bound veto-only receipt made component publication and downstream context objectively auditable without adding a generation route.
did_not_work: The first generic calculator goal did not pass existing requirement planning, and the supported Notes CLI run stopped when Qwen could not satisfy the existing split-test anchor after bounded repair.
experiments: Resume a comparable supported project at the tests component and measure whether the aggregate receipt is produced before post-build while keeping the current strict test-anchor validator.
